sections.h1:
A brand that matches
what you've actually built.
sections.lead: Logo systems, visual identity, and guidelines for companies whose product has outgrown the branding they launched with — built to hold up in a product UI, not just on a title slide.

sections.body: Radiant designs visual identities for technology companies: logo systems, typography and colour, brand guidelines, social and launch assets, and the brand-level design system that keeps it consistent across product and marketing. [PLACEHOLDER: name identity clients and one proof point, e.g. "Hawala: fintech identity from scratch; Lumen: luxury real estate brand".]

sections.label: Branding & Visual Identity
sections.challenge: Your product has evolved past the brand you launched with. The quick logo and default palette from year one don't reflect the quality of what you've built. Investors, partners, and customers see the gap — even if they don't say it.

cards.title: It works on the logo, not in the product
cards.body: A palette chosen for a presentation fails the first accessibility check inside a dense interface. We design identities against real product screens from the start.

cards.title: You look like every competitor
cards.body: The same gradient, the same three icons, the same stock geometry. We find the one property your category has abandoned and build the identity on it.

cards.title: The guidelines get ignored
cards.body: A 90-page PDF nobody opens is not governance. We ship guidelines as working files and templates, so following the brand is the fastest path for your team.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.title: Position before pixels
steps.body: We establish what the brand must signal, to whom, and against which competitors. You approve a written direction before we show a single mark.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.title: Build the system
steps.body: Logo system, type, colour, imagery, and motion, each tested on the surfaces you actually use — product UI, website, deck, app icon, social. Reviewable work every 48 hours.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.title: Ship it everywhere
steps.body: Guidelines, working templates, and launch assets, plus the brand-level tokens that connect the identity to your product design system.

sections.heading: Trusted by our partners
sections.name: Aaron D.
sections.quote: Radiant exceeded all our expectations! Design and animations quality are on top level.

cards.title: How much does a brand identity cost?
cards.body: A focused identity for an early-stage company starts at [PLACEHOLDER: price]. A full rebrand across product, site, and collateral is [PLACEHOLDER: range]. Scope is driven by surfaces, not by number of logo options.

cards.title: How long does a rebrand take?
cards.body: A startup identity takes four to six weeks. A rebrand that has to roll out across product, website, and sales material runs eight to twelve, usually phased so nothing launches half-changed.

cards.title: Do we need a full rebrand or a refresh?
cards.body: If your positioning still holds and only the execution is dated, a refresh is cheaper and lower-risk. We say so when that is the honest answer, after looking at what you have.

cards.title: Do you do naming?
cards.body: [PLACEHOLDER: confirm. If yes: naming, domain checks, and a shortlist tested against your market. If no: we partner with naming specialists and design around the name you choose.]

cards.title: Do you handle trademark checks?
cards.body: We run informal availability checks during exploration and flag risks early, but we are designers, not counsel. Final clearance goes through your trademark lawyer.

cards.title: Can you roll the brand into our product?
cards.body: Yes — that is usually where the value is. We connect brand tokens to the product design system so the identity holds in the interface, not only in marketing.

sections.label: Next step
sections.challenge: Send your current brand and a screen of your product. We will tell you whether you need a refresh or a rebrand, and what each would take.
